title: Send Email with JavaMailSender
summary: Configure SMTP, send plain-text messages, and distinguish submission from actual delivery.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Send Email Using Spring Boot | Gmail SMTP | Java Mail Sender

richText: Submit email through SMTP
SMTP is the protocol used to submit email to a mail server. JavaMailSender connects Spring code to that server.
Add spring-boot-starter-mail. With the mail libraries and spring.mail.host configured, Boot can create a JavaMailSender bean.
Use SimpleMailMessage for plain text. Use MimeMessage and MimeMessageHelper for HTML or attachments.
These examples use Spring Boot 3, Spring Framework 6, and Java 17. Boot 3 uses Jakarta Mail APIs when direct mail types are needed.
A weekly journal digest is one use case. Calculate the summary in a service, then pass the recipient, subject, and summary to the mail service.
Configure authentication and timeouts
The following properties describe an SMTP server that supports authenticated STARTTLS on port 587. STARTTLS upgrades the connection to TLS. Use the settings required by your provider.
Require the TLS upgrade so credentials are not sent over an unencrypted connection. Keep normal certificate validation enabled.
MAIL_USERNAME and MAIL_PASSWORD are environment variables. For Gmail, account policy may require an app password or OAuth. A normal account password is not a universal SMTP credential.
Connection, read, and write timeouts prevent a scheduled task or request thread from waiting indefinitely.
Send a plain-text digest
Inject JavaMailSender through the constructor. Use a configured sender address permitted by the mail provider.
The recipient comes from an authorized user record. Do not expose this method through an unauthenticated endpoint that accepts arbitrary recipients.
Separate submission from delivery
When send returns, SMTP submission completed without a reported error. It does not prove inbox delivery. A later bounce, spam filter, or provider rejection can still prevent delivery.
Allow MailException to reach the caller when it must retry or mark work as failed. Logging and returning normally would make a Kafka listener appear successful.
Retry temporary failures with a limit. Invalid recipients and rejected credentials need a correction, not endless retries.
A timeout can occur after the mail server accepted the email. Retrying can send a duplicate. Track a digest ID and delivery state, and document any remaining ambiguity.
Use a queue for large batches so one HTTP request does not send hundreds of emails. Keep recipient lists and message content out of normal logs.
